chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'What do you say about a man who puts the matter of his wife in her hand (giving her the choice of divorce)?' He said, 'The matter was assumed by one who is not its rightful authority, and he contradicted the Sunnah, and he did not validate the marriage.'

key_terms.أَمْرُ امْرَأَتِهِ: The matter/authority of his wife (referring to the right of divorce)
key_terms.بِيَدِهَا: In her hand (idiom for granting authority/choice)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a husband giving his wife the right to unilateral divorce?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that if a man grants his wife the unilateral right to divorce (takhliq) but she is not truly fit or appropriate for this authority, the act is considered a deviation from the Sunnah and the divorce is not deemed valid. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the condition of 'ahl' (fitness/competence) in the exercise of delegated rights, ensuring the wife's choice is genuine and legally sound within the marital contract.
